title: dedicated-autoscaler-throughput-burst-controls-util-reporting-v2
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves Dedicated autoscaler smoothing and burst controls, adds per-fleet throughput guarantees and richer utilization reporting. Backwards compatible flag-controlled rollout.
description:
Motivation: Several fleets observed oscillatory scaling and burst overruns during mixed-latency workloads. This PR introduces a second-generation smoothing controller for the Dedicated fleet autoscaler, tighter burst token-bucket accounting, and richer utilization reporting that ties observed throughput to SLA guarantees.

What this changes: - Implement a smoothed target calculation that uses EWMA of observed throughput and request queueing to avoid aggressive scale-ups/downs. - Add token-bucket burst controls at the fleet and node-pool levels with configurable burst budgets and decay windows. - Emit new observability metrics: dedicated.autoscaler.target_smoothed, dedicated.autoscaler.burst_tokens, dedicated.fleet.throughput_sla_ratio, and dedicated.fleet.utilization_p95. - Add an optional throughput_guarantee config per-fleet that allows ops teams to reserve baseline capacity for critical customers. - Update the Dedicated autoscaler config schema and documentation.

Compatibility and rollout: All changes are behind a feature flag (autoscaler.v2_smoothing). Existing fleets keep the current autoscaler until the flag is enabled. The throughput_guarantee defaults to null (no guarantee) and is only honored if explicitly set.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for smoothing math and token-bucket edge cases included. Integration test harness added to perf-canary that simulates bursty traffic and validates no SLA regressions. We ran the canary against three mid-sized fleets for 48 hours and observed 22% lower churn and no customer-facing latency regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Design sign-off (ENG-2345) - [x] Tests added - [x] Perf canary run - [x] Observability dashboards updated - [x] Docs updated (redwood-docs)

Related: Follow-up PR will expose a per-tenant API to request temporary burst boosts (RFC in ENG-2410).

b3e7d1a: add token-bucket implementation and node-pool accounting

e55b7f0: perf-canary integration and canary tests
patch_snippets:
--- a/redwood/services/dedicated/autoscaler/controller.py
+++ b/redwood/services/dedicated/autoscaler/controller.py
@@ def compute_target(self, history):
-    raw = history.recent_throughput() * scale_factor
-    return int(max(1, raw))
+    ewma = self._ewma_update(history.recent_throughput())
+    smoothed = max(1, int(math.ceil(ewma * self.scale_factor)))
+    return smoothed
--- a/redwood/services/dedicated/autoscaler/token_bucket.py
+++ b/redwood/services/dedicated/autoscaler/token_bucket.py
@@ class TokenBucket:
-    def add_tokens(self, n):
-        self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + n)
+    def add_tokens(self, n):
+        # decay window applied per-node to avoid global burst exhaustion
+        decayed = self._apply_decay(self.tokens)
+        self.tokens = min(self.capacity, decayed + n)
